name: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF
description: Tracks the S&P 500 index, holding roughly 500 of the largest US companies weighted by market capitalization, spanning technology, financials, healthcare and other sectors.
typical_holders: A default core holding across 401(k) and IRA retirement accounts, robo-advisor model portfolios, and institutional asset allocators seeking simple US large-cap exposure.
success_factors: One of the lowest expense ratios in the industry (0.03%), very high trading liquidity, and a straightforward pitch as a proxy for the overall US large-cap market have made it a go-to core holding.
political_context: Sensitive to Federal Reserve interest-rate policy, US corporate tax legislation, and antitrust or AI-regulation scrutiny of the mega-cap technology names that dominate its top holdings.

name: iShares Core S&P 500 ETF
description: Also tracks the S&P 500; functionally near-identical in holdings and weighting to VOO and SPY, differing mainly in issuer and minor structural details.
typical_holders: Heavily used in advisory model portfolios and institutional mandates, partly on the strength of BlackRock's distribution reach.
success_factors: BlackRock's scale, a 0.03% expense ratio, and deep institutional adoption drive its size.
political_context: Shares the same monetary-policy and mega-cap regulatory exposure as other S&P 500 trackers; BlackRock's own political visibility (ESG-investing debates, state-level divestment actions against the firm) is occasionally a talking point distinct from the fund's actual holdings.

name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
description: The original S&P 500 ETF, launched in 1993 and structured as a unit investment trust rather than an open-end fund, which changes how dividends are handled versus VOO/IVV.
typical_holders: The preferred vehicle for institutional and derivatives traders (options and futures markets are built around SPY specifically), alongside broad retail use.
success_factors: First-mover advantage and the deepest options/futures-linked liquidity of any ETF in the world keep it dominant despite a higher 0.09% fee than its Vanguard/iShares peers.
political_context: As the most widely quoted 'the market' proxy in financial media, its price action is routinely cited in political commentary on the economy; carries the same Fed-policy and corporate-tax sensitivities as other S&P 500 funds.

name: Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF
description: Tracks the CRSP US Total Market Index, covering nearly the entire investable US stock market — large-, mid-, small- and micro-cap companies — not just the largest 500.
typical_holders: A staple of Vanguard's popular three-fund portfolio strategy, widely used by long-term retail buy-and-hold investors and robo-advisors.
success_factors: A 0.03% expense ratio and 'own the whole market in one fund' simplicity have made it a favorite core holding.
political_context: Broader exposure than the S&P 500 adds sensitivity to policy affecting smaller domestic companies — small-business tax and credit conditions — alongside the usual mega-cap regulatory and monetary-policy factors.

name: Invesco QQQ Trust
description: Tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index: the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq, heavily concentrated in technology, communication services and consumer discretionary names.
typical_holders: Popular with both long-term tech investors and active/short-term traders; one of the most heavily traded ETFs in the world by dollar volume.
success_factors: Concentration in mega-cap tech and AI-related winners has driven strong long-term performance, and deep intraday liquidity makes it a favorite trading vehicle.
political_context: Highly exposed to antitrust and AI-regulation debates in Washington and Brussels, US-China technology export controls and tariffs, and Fed policy given growth stocks' sensitivity to interest rates.

name: iShares Core MSCI EAFE ETF
description: Tracks large- and mid-cap companies across developed markets in Europe, Australasia and the Far East (EAFE) — developed markets outside the US and Canada.
typical_holders: A standard building block for international-equity allocations in target-date funds and diversified model portfolios.
success_factors: A low 0.07% fee and broad developed-market diversification make it a default international-equity holding.
political_context: Exposed to European Central Bank and Bank of Japan monetary policy, EU fiscal and energy policy, and currency-translation effects from US dollar strength or weakness against the euro and yen.

name: Vanguard FTSE Developed Markets ETF
description: A similar mandate to IEFA — developed-market equities outside the US — but tracks a FTSE index and, unlike IEFA, includes Canada.
typical_holders: The natural international-equity pairing to VOO/VTI for investors building a simple, low-cost global portfolio.
success_factors: Vanguard's low-cost positioning (0.05%) and its role as a core international building block drive adoption.
political_context: Shares developed-market monetary-policy and currency exposure with IEFA; Canadian inclusion adds sensitivity to US-Canada trade policy and commodity/energy price swings.

name: Vanguard Growth ETF
description: Tracks the CRSP US Large Cap Growth Index — large US companies classified as 'growth' stocks, skewed toward technology and consumer names with high expected earnings growth.
typical_holders: Used by investors wanting a growth tilt on top of core index holdings without picking individual stocks.
success_factors: Low cost and heavy overlap with mega-cap tech winners have delivered strong recent performance.
political_context: Concentrated growth/tech exposure makes it sensitive to interest-rate expectations — growth stocks are more rate-sensitive than value — plus the same antitrust and AI-policy debates affecting QQQ.

name: Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF
description: Tracks a broad, float-adjusted index of US investment-grade government, agency, mortgage-backed and corporate bonds.
typical_holders: The default core bond holding in balanced portfolios for retail investors, target-date funds, and conservative institutional allocators.
success_factors: Extremely low cost (0.03%) and one-fund access to the entire investment-grade US bond market.
political_context: Directly and immediately sensitive to Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions, US Treasury issuance, federal deficit and debt-ceiling politics, and inflation data releases.

name: Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF
description: Tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index, screening for US companies with a decade-plus record of consistent dividend payments and strong quality/profitability metrics.
typical_holders: A favorite among income-seeking retail investors, particularly those using Schwab brokerage accounts where it trades commission-free.
success_factors: A reputation for durable, quality dividend payers plus a low 0.06% fee has made it one of the most popular dividend-focused ETFs.
political_context: Its financials- and industrials-heavy tilt makes it sensitive to bank regulation, interest-rate policy (which affects dividend stocks' relative appeal versus bonds), and US tax policy on dividends.

name: iShares Core MSCI Emerging Markets ETF
description: Tracks large-, mid- and small-cap companies across emerging markets including China, India, Taiwan, South Korea and Brazil.
typical_holders: Used by institutional allocators and diversified retail portfolios to add emerging-market growth exposure alongside developed-market holdings.
success_factors: Broad, low-cost (0.09%) access to emerging-market growth in a single fund.
political_context: Highly exposed to US-China trade and tariff policy, Chinese regulatory actions on domestic tech and property sectors, and broader emerging-market currency and capital-control risk.

name: iShares Core U.S. Aggregate Bond ETF
description: Tracks the same broad US investment-grade bond universe as BND — government, agency, mortgage-backed and corporate debt.
typical_holders: A default core bond holding for institutions and retail investors alike, often used interchangeably with BND.
success_factors: First-mover brand recognition as 'the' aggregate bond ETF, deep liquidity, and BlackRock's distribution scale.
political_context: Same Federal Reserve policy, Treasury issuance, and deficit/debt-ceiling sensitivities as BND.

name: Vanguard Value ETF
description: Tracks the CRSP US Large Cap Value Index — large US companies classified as 'value' stocks, typically trading at lower valuation multiples and skewed toward financials, healthcare and energy.
typical_holders: Used by investors seeking lower-volatility, income-oriented exposure, and often rotated into during periods of rising rates or growth-stock weakness.
success_factors: A low 0.04% fee and a straightforward value tilt for investors wary of growth-stock concentration risk.
political_context: Financials and energy weighting make it sensitive to bank regulation, interest-rate policy, and energy/climate policy affecting oil and gas producers.

name: Vanguard Total International Stock ETF
description: Tracks nearly the entire investable stock market outside the US, spanning both developed and emerging markets in one fund.
typical_holders: The natural pairing with VTI for investors following Vanguard's simple total-market portfolio approach.
success_factors: Single-fund simplicity for 'everything except the US' international exposure at a low 0.05% fee.
political_context: Combines the sensitivities of both developed-market funds (ECB/BOJ policy, European fiscal policy) and emerging-market funds (US-China trade tensions, EM currency and regulatory risk).

name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
description: Tracks a FTSE index of large- and mid-cap emerging-market companies; notably excludes South Korea, which FTSE classifies as developed — a key difference from IEMG's MSCI-based index.
typical_holders: Used similarly to IEMG by diversified retail and institutional portfolios seeking emerging-market exposure.
success_factors: Low-cost (0.07%) emerging-market access and Vanguard's brand trust with long-term index investors.
political_context: Same US-China trade policy and Chinese regulatory exposure as IEMG, with the South Korea exclusion slightly changing the country-risk balance.

name: SPDR Gold Shares
description: Holds physical gold bullion in vaults; each share represents a fractional ownership claim on that gold, giving investors direct price exposure without owning metal themselves.
typical_holders: Used by institutional allocators and central-bank-adjacent investors for portfolio hedging, as well as retail investors seeking inflation or crisis protection.
success_factors: First-mover status (launched 2004), deep liquidity, and gold's traditional role as an inflation hedge and safe haven have sustained demand, despite a 0.40% fee that's high for a passive product.
political_context: Extremely sensitive to Federal Reserve interest-rate policy (gold pays no yield, so it competes with bonds), US dollar strength, inflation expectations, and geopolitical crises or sanctions that drive safe-haven and central-bank gold-buying tied to de-dollarization politics.

name: iShares Russell 1000 Growth ETF
description: Tracks the Russell 1000 Growth Index — large- and mid-cap US growth stocks — similar in spirit to VUG but built on a different index methodology and reconstitution schedule.
typical_holders: Heavily used institutionally, since the Russell 1000 Growth index is a standard performance benchmark for active growth-fund managers.
success_factors: Long track record, deep liquidity, and status as a standard institutional benchmark.
political_context: Same tech/growth-stock rate sensitivity and antitrust/AI-regulation exposure as QQQ and VUG.

name: iShares Core S&P Mid-Cap ETF
description: Tracks the S&P MidCap 400 Index — US companies too large to be small-cap but not yet in the S&P 500, often described as established-but-still-growing businesses.
typical_holders: Used by diversified portfolios to fill the market-cap gap between S&P 500 and small-cap funds.
success_factors: Fills the 'mid-cap gap' at a low 0.05% fee, popular for diversification across the market-cap spectrum.
political_context: More domestically focused than mega-cap funds, so it's especially sensitive to US GDP growth, small-business lending conditions, and domestic fiscal policy rather than global trade tensions.

name: Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF
description: Tracks companies with a record of consistently increasing — not just paying — their dividend each year for at least a decade, skewing toward stable, established businesses.
typical_holders: Popular with income investors seeking lower volatility than the broad market, particularly those closer to or in retirement.
success_factors: A quality/stability tilt plus dividend growth appeals to income investors, at a low 0.05% fee.
political_context: Similar interest-rate sensitivity to other dividend-focused funds — bonds become more competitive with dividend stocks as rates rise — plus sector-specific regulatory exposure depending on top holdings.

name: iShares Core S&P Small-Cap ETF
description: Tracks the S&P SmallCap 600 Index — small US companies that must meet a profitability screen, unlike some small-cap indexes that include unprofitable firms.
typical_holders: Used by investors wanting small-cap exposure with a quality/profitability filter rather than the broadest possible small-cap universe.
success_factors: The profitability screen has historically helped it avoid some weaker performers common in small-cap indexes, at a low 0.06% fee.
political_context: Small caps are generally more domestically focused and sensitive to US interest rates (higher borrowing costs hit smaller firms harder), domestic fiscal stimulus, and small-business regulatory or tax policy.
